sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry confirmed surface expression of HA-ACKR2 in stable clones (L1/L2); functional assays with the tagged construct are not described in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: ACKR2 has no signal peptide (raw topology begins O, not S), so the N-terminus (residues 1–46) is directly extracellular; insert_after_residue = 0 places the tag before residue 1 (M), the sole extracellular N-terminus. L1 explicitly states 'extreme N-terminus' for a full-length, membrane-anchored construct, leaving exactly one possible junction; the position is therefore topology-derived rather than residue-validated. The 46-residue extracellular N-terminal domain provides ample space for a ~15–23 aa epitope tag, and TM1 begins only at residue 47, well beyond the ≥3-residue clearance requirement. Python verification confirms seq[0] = M and seq[46] = V (TM1 start). Full-length human ACKR2 stably expressed in mammalian cells with an HA tag (MYPYDVPDYAG) introduced at the extreme N-terminus by PCR; surface expression of the tagged receptor confirmed by flow cytometry in stable clones. L2 (same paper) corroborates the same construct and assay. L3 (PMC9723398) independently reports HA-tagged ACKR2 used for conditional surface expression studies in HEK293 T-Rex cells.

sources.claim: Nucleotides encoding an N-terminal HA tag (MYPYDVPDYAG) were introduced into human ACKR2 cDNA by PCR to generate HA-ACKR2 as described ( 44 ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are from the same paper (PMC4007430) and describe the identical HA-ACKR2 construct; L1 is the primary clip (explicit 'extreme N-terminus' and HA sequence), L2 is corroborating. L3 (PMC9723398) independently supports an N-terminal HA tag on full-length ACKR2 for surface expression studies but names no residue, so it reinforces rather than adds a second site. L4 (PMC5511891) reports a FLAG tag 'fused in frame' with full-length D6/ACKR2 but states no position (N-terminal vs. C-terminal); the C-terminus of ACKR2 (residues 316–384) is entirely intracellular, and without knowing which end carries the FLAG tag the site cannot be pinned to the extracellular face — L4 is therefore dropped per the 'tag position unstated' disqualification rule. No ledger line supports an internal loop insertion (ECL1, ECL2, or ECL3) for ACKR2.
